title: 2026-10-31_Linux_P2P_Ransom_Botnet_Investigation_3b2
description: Investigate a compromised system infected with the Linux P2P Ransom botnet ransomware, identify indicators of compromise, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The victim host in your network has been compromised by the Linux P2P Ransom botnet ransomware. This malware combines ransomware capabilities with botnet functionality, targeting Linux systems. It uses a peer-to-peer (P2P) network for communication and command and control (C2) purposes, making it resilient to traditional takedown methods.

Your task is to investigate the compromised system, identify the indicators of compromise, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access

levels.title: Identify the Command-and-Control Server
levels.content:
Identify the command-and-control server IP address used by the ransomware.

**Hint:** Check network connections and logs for suspicious outbound connections.

**Question:** What is the IP address of the command-and-control server?
levels.solution: To identify the command-and-control server IP address, you can check network connections and logs for suspicious outbound connections. Use commands like `netstat -tuln` or `ss -tuln` to list active connections. Additionally, check logs in `/var/log/` for any suspicious outbound connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for suspicious outbound connections in logs located in `/var/log/`.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `grep` to search for specific patterns in the logs that might indicate C2 communication.

levels.title: Determine the Command-and-Control Port
levels.content:
Determine which network port is used for suspicious command-and-control communication.

**Hint:** Investigate network traffic to identify unusual ports used by the ransomware.

**Question:** What is the port number used for command-and-control communication?
levels.solution: To determine the network port used for suspicious command-and-control communication, investigate network traffic using tools like `tcpdump` or `Wireshark`. Look for unusual ports that are actively being used for communication.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `tcpdump` to capture network traffic and identify unusual ports.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Analyze network traffic with `Wireshark` to find actively used ports.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Filter traffic by the suspicious IP address to narrow down the port used for C2 communication.

levels.title: Identify the Exfiltration Server
levels.content:
Identify the external host receiving sensitive data from the compromised system.

**Hint:** Analyze outbound network traffic to identify the exfiltration infrastructure.

**Question:** What is the IP address of the exfiltration server?
levels.solution: To identify the external host receiving sensitive data, analyze outbound network traffic using tools like `tcpdump` or `Wireshark`. Look for connections to external IPs that are receiving data from the compromised system.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `tcpdump` to capture outbound network traffic and identify external IPs.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Analyze network traffic with `Wireshark` to find connections to external hosts.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for large data transfers or unusual protocols that might indicate data exfiltration.
